Name: Capua, Capital of Campania: a Luxurious City and Hotbed of Rebellion
RagShortTexts: Capua is the second richest great city of the Italian peninsula after Rome, famed for its luxurious goods
After Cannae it changed sides and opened its gates to Hannibal's army, scheming to share mastery of the Italian peninsula
Rome besieged it cruelly behind a double ditch, and after the city fell it lost its self-government and became subject territory
BaseText: Capua (town_rome_neapolis, the area around modern Capua) lies in the heart of the volcanic plain of Campania, so fertile it seems to run with oil, and was the most prosperous great city of classical Italy after Rome and Syracuse. The city had a magnificent amphitheater and luxurious perfume and bronze workshops, and its goods were extremely plentiful. In 216 BC, after Cannae, Capua's ambitious nobles broke their treaty of alliance with Rome and opened the gates to Hannibal, even arrogantly demanding that after the war Capuan magistrates should take turns ruling Italy. Hannibal's army wintered and rested here, and it is said that 'the luxury of Capua dulled the blades of warriors of a hundred battles'. In 211 BC Fulvius and Appius besieged Capua with strong walls and ditches tens of miles long. After hunger forced it to surrender, Rome slaughtered the rebel senators and reduced the whole city to directly ruled territory without self-government.

Variants.Content: Capua's wealth far surpasses that of barbarous Rome, and we should have shared the Italian peninsula with Hannibal! Who could have known that the ditches of the Roman legions would strangle the life out of the whole city like chains.
City of traitors who broke their treaty! They led Hannibal into the plain of Campania, and today the axes of the Roman consuls are the most just sentence for those who break faith!
Capua's soft bed made our soldiers long for sweet wine and silken couches, but even more deadly was that we could not break through the Romans' double wall to rescue our ally.
